STEP 2 - Vessel: A large square white dinner plate, about 26 cm across. Since it is square, its area is closer to 26 × 26 ≈ 600 cm². To stay consistent with the method, I'll use the round-plate formula: 3.14 × 13² ≈ 530 cm².

STEP 3 - Items: Cheese pizza (crust, tomato sauce, melted cheese).

STEP 4 - Area: The pizza covers about 12% of the plate. Nothing else is on the plate, so the total food coverage is also about 12%.

STEP 5 - Volume: 0.12 × 530 ≈ 64 cm². At a typical height of about 1.2 cm, that gives 64 × 1.2 ≈ 76 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Using a bread-like slice density of 0.75 g/ml, 76 ml × 0.75 ≈ 57 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Cheese pizza is about 270 kcal per 100 g, so 57 g × 2.7 ≈ 154 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A full pizza slice is usually 100–120 g. What's left here looks like about half a slice, so roughly 57 g is plausible.
